question: Should OpenClaw elevate `message_sending` into the fail-closed universal outbound policy boundary, or introduce a new versioned outbound policy API with explicit trusted-plugin and audit semantics?
rationale: Source inspection proves remaining bypass and fail-open paths, but only maintainer product/security intent can decide permanent hook failure behavior, plugin authority, audit metadata, and which outbound sends are in scope.

options.title: Design a versioned policy API
options.body: Create a dedicated outbound policy contract that can be fail-closed, audited, scoped, and documented without overloading existing best-effort hook semantics.

options.title: Elevate message_sending
options.body: Make `message_sending` the universal exactly-once fail-closed gate and migrate all direct delivery paths onto that contract.

options.title: Keep hooks advisory
options.body: Document that strict DLP and compliance enforcement are not guaranteed by current hook surfaces and keep policy enforcement outside core for now.

recommendation.title: Design a versioned policy API
recommendation.body: Create a dedicated outbound policy contract that can be fail-closed, audited, scoped, and documented without overloading existing best-effort hook semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans security policy, audit semantics, and outbound architecture, where the history shows adjacent review and implementation involvement.
